raw_response:
I am getting old now, so I do not chase fancy ways. On my 8 mu, wheat and maize are still the main thing because that is the safest way here. Wheat feeds the family and brings steady money, and maize follows right after, so the land does not sit empty. Cotton I will only keep on a small piece, not much, because it takes more hand work and picking, and in my house there are only two of us. I learned long ago that if I spread myself too thin, I cannot manage any crop well.

For wheat, I will plant in early October like usual, around 5 mu. I will use a common improved local seed the dealers all sell, not the expensive kind. Before sowing I will put a base fertilizer, mainly nitrogen with some phosphorus, because wheat here cannot go without base manure. I usually do a bit more than the bare minimum, because if wheat stays yellow in spring, yield drops fast. If water is short I still try to irrigate at least at sowing, jointing, and filling. For summer maize, I will put it right in after wheat harvest on the same 5 mu. The turnaround is tight, so I will keep tillage simple and use quick field prep. Maize grows fast in summer, so if rain is decent I will not irrigate too much, maybe once or twice. I will use hybrid seed because maize seed is worth buying. For cotton, I will keep about 3 mu. Cotton gives cash, but it needs more looking after, more spraying, and more picking by hand. At my age, I cannot expand that. I will fertilize it, but not heavily, and I will irrigate only a couple of times if the weather turns dry.
